trust_decision.summary: Whether a plugin name (from a downloaded plugin.yaml, or from a CLI argument) may be joined onto the plugin root ~/.trivy/plugins to form a directory that is wiped, written, read or executed from; at the pinned commit nothing decides it, and the fix enforces it with os.Root confinement and filepath.IsLocal in Manager.install, Uninstall, load and loadMetadata.

landing_point.why: The summary says the plugin manager allows arbitrary file write; the obvious write is os.Create(filepath.Join(plugin.Dir(), configFile)) in Manager.install, where plugin.Dir() comes from the untrusted name set at pkg/plugin/manager.go:351.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:351 (loadMetadata sets plugin.dir from the stored plugin.yaml name rather than the directory name; reached from LoadAll pkg/plugin/manager.go:279 and load pkg/plugin/manager.go:325; the fix derives the directory from the directory name at fix.diff:403,423,461)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The installed plugin.yaml was written by Trivy itself and uninstall/info names are the local user's own CLI arguments, so a solver can argue only the freshly downloaded name in install() crosses a trust boundary and leave load/loadMetadata/Uninstall as they are.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The install argument is legitimately a path or URL containing '/' (e.g. `testdata/test_plugin`, GitHub archive URLs, `name@vX.Y.Z`), archives with a single top-level directory are unwrapped, and uninstalling a missing plugin must log 'No such plugin' and return nil; a fix that applies IsLocal to the src argument or errors on a missing name breaks these.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Platform.Bin from plugin.yaml is joined onto the plugin directory without confinement to form the executed file path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Bin names the plugin's own executable and the plugin author already gets code execution, and the advisory is about file write, not exec path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file, same package (pkg/plugin/plugin.go vs pkg/plugin/manager.go)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Plugin.Dir() falls back to TrivyHomeDir/plugins/p.Name when dir is unset; a caller that relies on the fallback reintroduces the name-to-path join outside the root.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fallback is still present upstream (latest/pkg/plugin/plugin.go:163-167), and a maintainer adding a helper that builds a Plugin from the index or from metadata without going through loadMetadata would naturally call Dir().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A cache of per-plugin index data or a downloaded per-plugin asset stored under indexPath's directory and keyed by the index entry name.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Update already writes into the plugin root through plain os/fsutils calls rather than the root, so a per-plugin cache next to index.yaml would be written the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An upgrade or rollback step that renames or backs up the old plugin directory using the newly downloaded name.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upgrade reinstalls from plugin.Repository and can receive a different name, so a backup/rename keyed on updated.Name is a natural addition.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal (untrusted metadata name joined to a managed directory; arbitrary write/delete)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject plugin.Name containing ".." (or call filepath.Base) in install() right after decoding the downloaded plugin.yaml, leaving Uninstall/load CLI names, the absolute and symlink shapes, and loadMetadata's stored-name dir derivation alone.

The O8 Bin route is an exec-path escape, not a write; its security value is debatable because a malicious plugin already runs code, so a hidden test demanding it may be judged unfair. Pattern B is weak.

O1 counts install, run, upgrade, uninstall, info, list/startup LoadAll, output plugin Start, and TRIVY_RUN_AS_PLUGIN; the write sink proper is reached by four of them (install, run, upgrade, TRIVY_RUN_AS_PLUGIN).

In normal flow the stored plugin.yaml name matches its directory, so the loadMetadata save/reload route matters mainly when the stored name diverges (manual edits, or upgrade receiving a different name); not proven exploitable within the time.
recall_risk is an estimate: the advisory was published 2026-08-18, after the knowledge cutoff, for a widely used project.
